title: A correspondent at Randan to the duc de Nevers, 27 March and 4 April 1587 (BnF fr. 3975 ff. 28, 30; DECODE R4285, R4286)

steps.what: BnF notice (cc504266) gives fr. 3975 pieces 7 (f. 28, 27 Mar 1587, 'avec chiffrement et déchiffrement', voyage to Lyon) and 8 (f. 30, 4 Apr 1587, same correspondent); Gallica ark btv1b90605473 found by SRU on dc.source; f. 28 = canvas 52, f. 30 = canvas 56.
Both letters mostly clear French: codes 94, 6, 23 on f. 28r, a ten-sign dateline on f. 28v, code 45 and a 13-sign run on f. 30r with glosses 'Le duc d'Espernon' and 'Lyon'.
Tomokiyo's league.htm: fr. 3975 has no cipher listed. Tomokiyo's nevers.htm catalogue of the fr. 3995 key book read for 1586-87 keys with numbered names.
fr. 3995 (btv1b525085665) canvases 20-80 fetched; key no. 10 (f. 21) ruled out (45 = Picardie).
Key no. 11 (f. 23) read: 45 = D. d'Espernon, 94 = Marquis, 6 = Mr d'Antragues, 23 = Rne de Navarre, and π ^ ꭓ é = Lyon; small-word capitals and the null rule tabulated (key.md).
Remaining run signs and the dateline enumerated over key values and nulls and scored with fr-1600-letters (enum_readings.py), then one- and two-edit variants (edits.py): no convincing French.

Tomokiyo's note that no. 11 is used in fr. 3413 f. 102 followed up (btv1b52510705j canvas 213): same hand and monogram as fr. 3975, dated Clermont 25 Feb [1586], five cipher lines with interlinear decipherment.
The glossed sibling aligned with the key gave the writer's glyph forms: Ŧ = p, capital F = et, 1 = d, 0/⊕ = e, 0 = s, 2/z one shape, ◊ = a.
Run re-read: Lyon [∞ ƥ] et ce pais ('passant pres Lyon et ce pais'); dateline: de [∞] Randan (de); dec.py writes reading.tsv.
Mémoires de M. le duc de Nevers (1665), Gallica full text for Randan, Chenonceau, Espernon: these letters not printed.
24 of 27 cipher units read as sense; ∞ a null by the key's rule; ƥ in the run and the dateline's trailing 'de' unexplained.

The three doubtful signs re-examined at 3x on the full-resolution scans: the dateline's last two (ι ⊕) are a pale false start struck through with '=', i.e. cancelled; the ƥ in the f. 30 run stays a probable null.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key no. 11 of the Nevers key book (BnF fr. 3995 f. 23), not tied to these letters by DECODE, the BnF or Tomokiyo, was found to fit after trying Tomokiyo's list of the fr. 3995 keys (no. 10 ruled out); the writer's glyph forms were calibrated on a glossed sibling letter, fr. 3413 f. 102.
outcome.fraction_read_source: nevers1587/reading.tsv: 27 cipher units, all given a key value, null or cancellation; 26 accounted for as sense (22 letters/words/codes, 3 nulls, 2 struck out), 1 doubtful (ƥ taken as a null)

gaps.item: f. 30 run, sign 6 (ƥ after the null ∞): key value a gives no sense, taken as a null
